_: Name, description and badge live in src/resources/connectors.json so the console and the browser process cannot disagree about them.

personal_token.label: API token
notes: Pylon does not publish a fixed prefix for its tokens, and the field is empty deliberately rather than forgotten.
Anything the token does is attributed in Pylon to the name of the token, not to a person. Name it 'Flux' so an audit log entry is traceable.
There is no scope selection. A token carries whatever its organisation permits, so the narrowing has to happen in Flux: only the read operations below are exposed.
RFC 6750 bearer auth, nothing more. No OAuth flow is published for the Pylon API.
GET /me is the documented way to confirm a token works - it returns the organisation the token belongs to.

pagination.request: cursor query parameter; limit defaults to 100 and must be greater than 0 and less than 1000

errors.shape: { errors: string[], request_id: string, exists_id?: string }
errors.note: Every response carries a request_id. Log it - it is what Pylon support asks for.
errors.403: The caller or organisation is not allowed to use that endpoint. Audit logs in particular are gated this way.

get_me.notes: Returns details about the organisation the token belongs to. The connect-time check.

get_account.notes: id may be the Pylon ID or an external ID.

search_accounts.notes: A POST that reads. search_text is fuzzy and is intersected with the filter. Filterable: id (equals/in/not_in), domains and tags (contains/does_not_contain/in/not_in), name (equals/in/not_in/string_contains), external_ids and owner_id (equals/in/not_in/is_set/is_unset). Custom fields are addressed by slug in field.

list_audit_logs.notes: Returns 403 unless the organisation is entitled to it.

search_audit_logs.notes: Filterable: action (equals/in/not_in/string_contains/string_does_not_contain), action_happened_at (time_is_after/time_is_before/time_range). Timestamps are RFC 3339.

get_contact.notes: id may be the Pylon ID or an external ID.

search_contacts.notes: Filterable: id and account_id (equals/in/not_in), email and name (equals/in/not_in/string_contains). Custom fields by slug in field. search_text is fuzzy and intersects the filter.

list_users.notes: Organisation members, not contacts. include_deactivated defaults to false.

search_users.notes: Only email is filterable, and only with equals/in/not_in.

get_call_recording.notes: Carries title, summary, participant_emails, duration_ms and a url. source names the recorder - fathom, gong, grain, granola or custom_call_recorder.

search_call_recordings.notes: Filterable: account_id (equals/in/not_in/is_set/is_unset), source (equals/in/not_in), title (equals/string_contains), start_time (time_is_after/time_is_before/time_range). Timestamps are RFC 3339. This one's limit is <= 1000, not < 1000 - the only endpoint read so far that differs.

list_issues.notes: start_time and end_time are REQUIRED and the span must be <= 30 days. There is no 'list everything' - a wider search has to be windowed, or use search_issues.

search_issues.notes: The practical way in, since it has no 30-day window. Filterable: created_at / resolved_at / updated_at / latest_message_activity_at (time ops), account_id / requester_id / assignee_id / ticket_form_id / issue_type (equals,in,not_in,is_set,is_unset), state / team_id / follower_user_id / follower_contact_id / slack_channel_id (equals,in,not_in), tags (contains,does_not_contain,in,not_in), title / body_html (string_contains,string_does_not_contain). Custom fields by slug in field; tags by name.

get_issue.notes: Accepts the ID or the issue number. The most generous limit on the API.

list_issue_statuses.notes: Resolve before filtering on state - the standard values are new, waiting_on_you, waiting_on_customer, on_hold and closed, but organisations define custom status slugs too.

get_issue_voice_calls.notes: Phone issues only. Returns recordings with parsed transcript segments and a PRESIGNED download URL for the audio. Recordings whose transcript has not finished are silently omitted - an empty result may mean 'not yet', not 'none', so refetch before concluding.

list_messages.notes: Oldest first, and includes both customer-visible replies and internal notes - is_private separates them. Omitting BOTH limit and cursor returns every message for backwards compatibility; passing a cursor without a limit gives pages of 100. On a long issue the default is therefore unbounded - pass a limit.

reply_to_issue.notes: Customer-facing - the requester sees this. message_id must be the TOP-LEVEL id from list_messages, not thread_id and not email_info.message_id, and it must point at a customer-visible message rather than an internal note. On an email conversation email_info must carry at least one recipient: the referenced message sets the threading headers but its recipients are NOT copied, so a reply with no recipients goes nowhere.

create_internal_note.notes: Internal only - the requester never sees it, which is why this is `draft` while reply_to_issue is `send`. Thread selection: thread_id posts to that thread; message_id posts to the thread holding that note; BOTH is a 400; neither falls back to the most recent Slack-backed internal thread, or creates a Pylon-only one named by thread_name. Note thread_id here is the thread's `id` field, NOT its `thread_id` field.

filters.note: Pylon's search endpoints share one filter object across resources, so this is worth knowing once.
rules: value is for single-valued operators, values for in and not_in.
subfilters are only valid under and / or, and the tree may be at most 3 deep.
Which fields are filterable is per endpoint - the shared operator list does not mean a field accepts all of them.

pending_operations.note: Issues and Messages are in - the two that mattered. What is left is peripheral to a support-triage task.

rate_limits.note: Per endpoint, not per account, and published on each endpoint rather than as one global figure. The pattern in what has been read: plain reads 60/min, searches 20/min, and anything expensive or destructive 10/min. Read the endpoint's own figure rather than assuming 60.

never_expose: POST /accounts/merge - permanently deletes the merged accounts, is explicitly not undoable, and is not transactional across the batch, so a failure halfway leaves the earlier merges done. Nothing in the Flux catalogue needs it.
PATCH /accounts - bulk-edits up to 100 accounts in one call, and tags default to replace rather than append.
PATCH /users/{id} - can change a colleague's role_id, which is a permissions change, not a data edit.
DELETE /issues/{id} and DELETE /issues/{id}/messages/{message_id} - both permanent, and deleting a message also deletes it in the connected external system, so it reaches outside Pylon.
POST /issues/{id}/messages/{message_id}/redact - permanently overwrites the stored content and deletes attachments by default. Explicitly not undoable.
POST /issues/{id}/external-issues - besides linking, it can flip the issue's status as a side effect (see gotchas).

POST /issues/{id}/ai-response - it invokes Pylon's own AI agent to draft a customer answer. Flux is already the agent; chaining a second one to write support replies is a strange loop, and the documentation does not say where the response lands when post_as_internal_note is false.
PATCH /issues/{id} - it can reassign the issue, change its team, retag it and move its state. Legitimate for a human, too blunt for a task.

notes: The base URL, the bearer scheme, every path and every rate limit above come out of the OpenAPI documents embedded in Pylon's own reference pages, which the user supplied. Nothing here is inferred from the resource index.
docs.usepylon.com is not reachable from the Flux container - the egress proxy refuses the CONNECT - so the remaining resources need their pages supplying the same way.

custom_apps.note: Not a Flux connector operation. Pylon Custom Apps run the other way round - Pylon GETs an endpoint you host and renders the JSON it returns in the issue sidebar. A desktop browser has no public endpoint, so Flux cannot be a custom app. Recorded so it is not mistaken for an API surface.
custom_apps.handshake: GET with request_type=verify and a one-time code; the endpoint must echo the code back, as JSON {"code":...} or as text/plain. Repeated whenever the app disconnects.
custom_apps.fetch: GET with request_type=fetch_data plus app_id, widget_id, issue_id, organization_id, account_id, requester_id and requester_email.
custom_apps.response: { version, header, components } where components are card, text, date_time, badge, button, link or divider. Badge colours are limited to blue, green, red, orange, gray.

gotchas: Pylon threads carry BOTH an `id` and a `thread_id`, and they are different values. create_internal_note wants the `id`; `thread_id` is the external chat platform's identifier. Getting this backwards is the most likely way to fail against this API.
reply_to_issue wants the message's top-level `id` - not `thread_id`, not the nested email_info.message_id (which is the provider's own). Three plausible identifiers on one object, one correct answer.
list_issues cannot list everything: a time range is mandatory and capped at 30 days. search_issues has no such window and is the right entry point for anything open-ended.
list_messages with neither limit nor cursor returns EVERY message on the issue, by design for backwards compatibility. Always pass a limit.
Rate limits vary per endpoint from 10/min to 60/min and the cheap ones are not the ones you would guess - get_issue is 60/min, list_issues is 10/min. Read the endpoint's own figure.
Linking an external issue can silently change the issue's status, if the connected app has 'automatically change issue status when linked' enabled. A link is not a read-only annotation.
